# Currency (Australian Coins) Determination 2019

made under the *Currency Act 1965*

**Compilation No. 106**

**Compilation date:** 30 September 2026

**Includes amendments:** *Currency (Australian Coins) Amendment (2026 Royal Australian Mint No. 10) Determination 2026*

This compilation is in 2 volumes

**Volume 1: sections 1–5**

**Schedules 2019 to 2023**

Volume 2: Schedule 2024 to 2026

Endnotes

Each volume has its own contents

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *Currency (Australian Coins) Determination 2019* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 30 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au). The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. For more information on any uncommenced amendments, see the Register for the compiled law.

**Application, saving and transitional provisions for provisions and amendments**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. For more information on any modifications, see the Register for the compiled law.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

Contents

### Part 1—Preliminary

###### 1 Name

This instrument is the *Currency (Australian Coins) Determination 2019*.

###### 3 Authority

This instrument is made under the *Currency Act 1965*.

###### 4 Definition

Note: Paragraph 13(1)(b) of the *Legislation Act 2003* has the effect that expressions have the same meaning in this instrument as in the *Currency Act 1965* as in force from time to time.

In this instrument:

***the Act*** means the *Currency Act 1965*.

### Part 2—Specifications for Australian Coins

###### 5 Specifications of denominations, standard compositions, standard weights, design and dimensions of coins

(1) For each item (the ***relevant item***) of a table in Division 1 of Part 1 or 2 of a Schedule to this instrument:

(a) subsection (2) of this section has effect for the purposes of paragraph 13(2)(b) of the Act; and

(b) subsection (3) of this section has effect for the purposes of section 13A of the Act.

(2) The Act is to have effect, on and after the day specified in the relevant item, as if:

(a) there were included in the Schedule to the Act a reference to the denomination of money specified in the relevant item; and

(b) there were specified in that Schedule opposite to that denomination, as the standard composition of coins of that denomination, the standard composition specified in the relevant item.

(3) The standard weight, the allowable variation from that standard weight, the design, and the dimensions, of a coin of the denomination specified in the relevant item are determined, on and after the day specified in the relevant item, to be those specified in the relevant item.

(4) Division 2 of Part 1 or 2 of a Schedule to this instrument has effect for the purposes of Division 1 of that Part.

#### Division 2—Explanation of symbols

###### 3 Symbols used in Division 1

Each item of the following table contains an explanation of a symbol used in Division 1 of this Schedule to describe the shape, edge design, obverse design and reverse design of a coin.

<tr>
<td>20</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O1</td>
<td>A design consisting of an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(d) “IRB”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>21</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O2</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) at the bottom of the face of the coin, a circle enclosing the following:<br>(i) an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II; and<br>(ii) “IRB”; and<br>(iii) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(iv) “AUSTRALIA 2019”; and<br>(v) in the background and enclosed by a circle, a partially obscured representation of a transcript; and<br>(b) a representation of the moon; and<br>(c) a representation of the Parkes radio telescope positioned on a stylised representation of a part of the planet Earth; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “FIVE DOLLARS”; and<br>(ii) “AWB”.</td>

<tr>
<td>18A</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O11</td>
<td colspan="2">A design consisting of an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(d) “JC”; and<br>(e) in the background, the equator, latitude lines, longitude lines and an ornamental pattern.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>19</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O12</td>
<td>A design consisting of an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(d) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(e) “JC”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>22</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O13</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central silver circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iii) “JC”; and<br>(b) surrounding that central circle, a copper ring bearing an ornamental Japanese pattern of arcs.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>23</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O14</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR” or “DOLLARS” as the case requires; and<br>(v) “JC”; and<br>(b) surrounding that central circle, an ornamental border comprising stylised representations of splashing water; and<br>(c) immediately inside the rim of the coin, a stylised representation of the following:<br>(i) a rat; and<br>(ii) a pig; and<br>(iii) a dog; and<br>(iv) a rooster; and<br>(v) a monkey; and<br>(vi) a goat; and<br>(vii) a horse; and<br>(viii) a snake; and<br>(ix) a dragon; and<br>(x) a rabbit; and<br>(xi) a tiger; and<br>(xii) an ox; and<br>(d) the animal mentioned in paragraph (c) that relates to the relevant zodiac year appearing at the top of the coin.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>24</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O15</td>
<td>A rectangular design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II; and<br>(b) surrounding the central circle, a stylised representation of willow branches; and<br>(c) curved convex border edges; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(v) “JC”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>25</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O16</td>
<td>A triangular design consisting of:<br>(a) in a corner of the triangle, an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) “JC”; and<br>(b) below the effigy, in the background, a stylised representation of a shipwreck, and survivors in a small boat in the ocean; and<br>(c) in the foreground, a man clinging to a cliff‑face, rocks, and a skeleton; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>26</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O17</td>
<td>The same as for item 25 except in paragraph (d) omit subparagraph (i) and substitute:<br>(i) “ONE DOLLAR”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>27</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O18</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II; and<br>(b) within the central circle, the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) “ONE OUNCE FINE SILVER”; and<br>(iv) “JC”; and<br>(c) surrounding the central circle, eight thick lines, stylised to represent planetary orbits; and<br>(d) fine textured lines; and<br>(e) representations of the following eight planets:<br>(i) Mercury; and<br>(ii) Venus; and<br>(iii) Earth, with its moon appearing on the left; and<br>(iv) Mars; and<br>(v) Jupiter; and<br>(vi) Saturn; and<br>(vii) Uranus; and<br>(viii) Neptune; and<br>(f) representations of five pointed stars; and<br>(g) dots, representing dwarf planets, exoplanets, meteorites and stars.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>28</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O19</td>
<td>The same as item 27, except omit subparagraph (b)(iii) and substitute:<br>(iii) “ONE OUNCE .9999 GOLD”; and</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>29</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O20</td>
<td>A triangular design, with an antiqued finish, consisting of:<br>(a) at the top of the face of the coin, a circle enclosing the following:<br>(i) an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II; and<br>(ii) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(iii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iv) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(v) “JC”; and<br>(b) in the background, a representation of a ship partially submerged in a body of water; and<br>(c) at the edge of that water, a representation of a man holding a sword and engaging in battle with a man holding a spear; and<br>(d) a representation of a woman standing on the beach and holding a baby; and<br>(e) in the foreground, a representation of a man holding a gun and engaging in battle with a man holding a spear; and<br>(f) a triangular border with rounded corners; and<br>(g) at the bottom of the face of the coin, a rectangular shape with rounded corners containing the inscription “ONE DOLLAR”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>30</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O21</td>
<td>A triangular design, with an antiqued finish, consisting of:<br>(a) at the top of the face of the coin, a circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) an amount in words, in dollars, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR” or “DOLLARS” as the case requires; and<br>(iv) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(v) “JC”; and<br>(b) immediately inside the rim of the coin, a stylised jagged border; and<br>(c) inside the border is a depiction of the sinking of the Vergulde Draeck including the depiction of an underwater scene of scattered coins and artefacts.</td>

<td>34</td>

<td>O3</td>
<td colspan="2">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR” or “DOLLARS” as the case requires; and<br>(v) “JC”; and<br>(b) surrounding that central circle, an ornamental border comprising stylised representations of splashing water; and<br>(c) immediately inside the rim of the coin, a stylised representation of the following:<br>(i) a rat; and<br>(ii) a pig; and<br>(iii) a dog; and<br>(iv) a rooster; and<br>(v) a monkey; and<br>(vi) a goat; and<br>(vii) a horse; and<br>(viii) a snake; and<br>(ix) a dragon; and<br>(x) a rabbit; and<br>(xi) a tiger; and<br>(xii) an ox; and<br>(d) the animal mentioned in paragraph (c) that relates to the relevant zodiac year appearing at the top of the coin.</td>

<tr>

<td>R3</td>
<td colspan="2">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a stylised representation of a Centurion tank with a soldier partly within the tank, and partly out, and holding a mounted gun; and<br>(b) next to the tank, a representation of a soldier holding a rifle at the ready; and<br>(c) beneath the tank, in the foreground, stylised jungle foliage; and<br>(d) at the top of the coin, a representation of a Bell UH‑1 Iroquois helicopter (also known as a “Huey”), viewed from the side with smoke billowing from the back of the helicopter body; and<br>(e) in the background, a stylised representation of a forest; and<br>(f) 2 perpendicular lines crossing at the bottom left of the coin; and<br>(g) the following:<br>(i) “50”; and<br>(ii) “THE BATTLE OF LONG KHANH”; and<br>(iii) “YS 507938” (which is the grid reference to the site of the Battle of Long Khanh fought on 6 and 7 June 1971); and<br>(iv) “AB” (in a stylised form).</td>
</tr>

<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a green ring with yellow stylised stars (4 of them 7-pointed and one 5-pointed) representing the constellation Crux (commonly known as the Southern Cross), partially obscured by a central circle; and<br>(b) within the central circle a stylised representation of the letter ‘S’; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “2022 COMMONWEALTH GAMES TEAM”; and<br>(ii) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>194</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R95</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a stylised representation of 6 athletes, with each athlete representing one of the following:<br>(i) a diver, in mid-dive, over 2 wavy lines, representing water; and<br>(ii) a beach volleyball player ‘digging’; and<br>(iii) a mountain biker wearing a helmet, on 2 circles representing a bike riding down a jiggered line, representing an uneven slope; and<br>(iv) a cricket player, holding a cricket bat in mid-shot next to cricket stumps; and<br>(v) the torso of a swimmer, mid-stroke, above a curved line representing water; and<br>(vi) a boxer, wearing gloves, in a punching action; and<br>(b) the following:<br>(i) “2022 AUSTRALIAN COMMONWEALTH GAMES TEAM”; and<br>(ii) “INTEGRITY”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>195</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R96</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a stylised representation of 7 athletes, with each athlete representing one of the following:<br>(i) an artistic gymnast competing; and<br>(ii) the torso of a netball player shooting a netball into a representation of a netball hoop; and<br>(iii) a road cyclist, wearing a helmet on 2 circles representing a bicycle; and<br>(iv) a rugby player, running and holding a rugby ball; and<br>(v) a squash player, holding a squash racquet and hitting a squash ball; and<br>(vi) 2 wrestlers, wrestling; and<br>(b) the following:<br>(i) “2022 AUSTRALIAN COMMONWEALTH GAMES TEAM”; and<br>(ii) “RESPECT”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>196</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R97</td>

<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td>R98</td>

<td></td>

<td>20</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O1</td>
<td colspan="2">A design consisting of a circle immediately inside the rim that surrounds an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars and cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(d) “JC”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>21</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O2</td>
<td colspan="2">A design consisting of a circle immediately inside the rim that surrounds an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(c) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(d) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars and cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(e) “JC”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>22</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O3</td>
<td colspan="2">A design consisting of a circle immediately inside the rim that surrounds an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars and cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(d) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(e) “Xoz 9999 Au” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(f) “JC”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>25</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O6</td>
<td colspan="2">The same as for item 22, except omit paragraph (e) and substitute:<br>(e) “Xoz 9999 Ag” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and</td>
</tr>

<td>O10</td>

<tr>

<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O3</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(v) “JC”; and<br>(b) surrounding that central circle, an ornamental border comprising stylised representations of splashing water; and<br>(c) immediately inside the rim of the coin, a stylised representation of the following:<br>(i) a rat; and<br>(ii) a pig; and<br>(iii) a dog; and<br>(iv) a rooster; and<br>(v) a monkey; and<br>(vi) a goat; and<br>(vii) a horse; and<br>(viii) a snake; and<br>(ix) a dragon; and<br>(x) a rabbit; and<br>(xi) a tiger; and<br>(xii) an ox; and<br>(d) the animal mentioned in paragraph (c) that relates to the relevant zodiac year appearing at the top of the coin.</td>
</tr>

</tr>
<tr>

<td colspan="2">O11</td>

</tr>

<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O15</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) at the bottom of the coin, a circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II; and<br>(b) the following:<br>(i) ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) “JC”; and<br>(c) above the effigy, a representation of the male lion depicted on the Coat of Arms of New South Wales sitting on its haunches; and<br>(d) in the background, 4 representations of 8-pointed stars (as depicted in the Coat of Arms of New South Wales), each partially obscured, and 8 stylised Tudor roses are positioned on and around the St George’s Cross (as depicted on the English flag); and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “X OUNCE.9999 Au” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(ii) “NEWLY RISEN”; and<br>(iii) “HOW BRIGHTLY”; and<br>(iv) “YOU SHINE”.</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>100</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R1</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) at the top centre of the coin, a stylised representation of St Edward’s Crown; and<br>(b) 69 additional, partially obscured St Edward’s Crowns, in a repeated overlaid patterned, forming an arc over the top of the coin; and<br>(c) in the centre, the Royal cypher of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II, and<br>(d) at the bottom, a stylised representation of lily of the valley and golden wattle flowers, with foliage, surrounding the cypher; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “PLATINUM”; and<br>(ii) “JUBILEE”; and<br>(iii) “BS”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>101</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R2</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the background, a semicircular pink, blue and white coloured pattern of 9 segments depicting a Ferris wheel with 9 stylised carriages,<br>(b) partially obscuring the Ferris wheel, a representation of the following:<br>(i) a horse; and<br>(ii) a chicken; and<br>(iii) a sheep; and<br>(iv) a woven basket with produce spilling forth, including pumpkins, sunflowers, pears, grapes and apples; and<br>(v) ears of wheat; and<br>(vi) a tractor; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “200 YEARS”; and<br>(ii) “ROYAL AGRICULTURAL SOCIETIES AND SHOWS”; and<br>(iii) “TD”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>102</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R3</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a stylised representation of a winner’s rosette with 8 ribboned sections representing the 8 State and Territory Royal agricultural societies of Australia, with each ribboned section depicting one of the following elements of agricultural shows:<br>(i) a side‑on representation of a cow and a sheep with a winner’s ribbon draped on each animal; and<br>(ii) a stylised representation of 2 bumper cars, with one numbered “5” in the foreground and one numbered “6” in the background; and<br>(iii) a stylised representation of a first prize rosette with 3 ribbon tails in front of a side‑on rooster; and<br>(iv) stylised representation of a man, standing on a springboard, holding an axe and chopping a tree pole in a wood chopping competition; and<br>(v) a stylised representation of a larger tractor partially obscured by a smaller tractor; and<br>(vi) a stylised representation of a line of laughing sideshow clowns, extending into the background; and<br>(vii) a stylised representation of a horse and rider jumping over a show jumping jump; and<br>(viii) a stylised representation of a show ride, partially obscured by a crowd; and<br>(b) the following:<br>(i) “BICENTENARY”; and<br>(ii) “ROYAL AGRICULTURAL SOCIETIES AND SHOWS”; and<br>(iii) “TD”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>103</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R4</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the background, a stylised representation of a crowd of supporters cheering, 2 are holding scarves, 2 are holding flags, and 3 standing up with their arms outstretched; and<br>(b) in the foreground and partially obscuring the crowd, a stylised representation of a supporter holding a scarf; and<br>(c) amongst the crowd, stylised representations of stadium seats; and<br>(d) in the foreground, on the bottom right of the coin, a stylised representation of a letter ‘A’; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “AUSSIE AUSSIE AUSSIE”; and<br>(ii) “OI OI OI”; and<br>(iii) “1 DOLLAR”.</td>
</tr>

<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R5</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of 2 bushrangers on horseback; and<br>(b) in the background, a silhouette of a man on horseback, partially obscuring a silhouette of a stylised representation of Australian bushland; and<br>(c) in the foreground, at the bottom right of the coin, a stylised representation of a letter “B”; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “BUSHRANGERS”; and<br>(ii) “1 DOLLAR”.</td>

WILLIAMS”; and<br>(ii) “1 DOLLAR”.</td>

<td colspan="2">R16</td>

<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a stylised representation of a horned jumbuck with textured fleece standing facing forward and on a stylised representation of grass; and<br>(b) in the background on the left of the coin, a stylised representation of a windmill; and<br>(c) in the foreground on the bottom right of the coin, a stylised representation of a letter ‘J’; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “JUMBUCK”; and<br>(ii) “1 DOLLAR”.</td>
</tr>

</tr>

<td colspan="2">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the background, a representation of goal posts from an Australian Football League (<b><i>AFL</b></i>) playing field; and<br>(b) in the foreground, partially obscuring the goal posts, is a representation of the 2023 AFL Premiership Cup; and<br>(c) emanating from base of the Cup, a pattern of lines radiating to each side, and to the bottom, of the coin; and<br>(d) tied to the handles of the Cup, stylised representations of ribbons; and<br>(e) below the Cup, a coloured representation of the logo of the AFL; and<br>(f) the following:<br>(i) “2023 AFL PREMIERSHIP SEASON”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIAN FOOTBALL LEAGUE 2023 PREMIERSHIP CUP”.</td>
<td></td>

<td>A design consisting of a circle immediately inside the rim that surrounds an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars and cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(d) “JC”.</td>

<td>O2</td>

<td>143</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R44</td>
<td>A design consisting of a circular border immediately inside the rim that surrounds a stylised representation of a flame of remembrance that is partially obscuring a wreath of poppies, and the following:<br>(a) “25 APRIL”; and<br>(b) “LEST WE FORGET” and<br>(c) “WR” and<br>(d) “P”</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>144</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R45</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the background, stylised representations of branches with leaves and flowers (3 of the flowers with inset diamonds); and<br>(b) in the foreground, partially obscuring the branches, a stylised representation of a snake wrapped around another branch (also with leaves and flowers), as an attached piece with inset diamonds; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “THE JEWELLED SNAKE”; and<br>(ii) the Chinese language character (蛇) pronounced <i>shé</i> under the Pinyin system and meaning snake; and<br>(iii) “SR”; and<br>(iv) “P”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>145</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R46</td>
<td>A design consisting of a landscape featuring grassy flatlands, boab trees, termite mounds, rock formations, and a diamond inset surrounded by stylised sunrays extending out to form a circle, and the following:<br>(a) “KIMBERLEY SUNRISE”; and<br>(b) “2023”; and<br>(c) “Xoz 9999 GOLD” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals)<br>(d) “TV”; and<br>(e) “P”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>146</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R47</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the background, a stylised representation of stones in a pond; and<br>(b) partially obscuring the stones, a stylised representation of 3 koi fish swimming amongst water lilies; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “KOI”; and<br>(ii) “2023”; and<br>(iii) “X KILO 9999 SILVER” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(iv) “NM”; and<br>(v) “P”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>147</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R48</td>
<td>The same as for item 130, except for the following:<br>(a) in paragraph (b) of that item, omit “grass trees”, substitute “a grass tree”; and<br>(b) omit subparagraph (c)(iii) and substitute:<br>(iii) “Xg 9999 GOLD” (where “X” is the nominal weight in grams of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(c) omit subparagraphs (c)(v) and (vi), and substitute:<br>(v) “P”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>148</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R49</td>
<td>A design, superimposed over radial lines, consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a representation of a kangaroo facing its joey, both standing on their hindlegs; and<br>(b) in the background, representations of plants, rocks and a small grassy escarpment; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “JM”; and<br>(ii) “P”; and<br>(iii) a microscopic “P”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>149</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R50</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a representation of a dragon and a koi fish encircling a flaming pearl; and<br>(b) in the background, a stylised representation of a bridge over a river, a grassy riverbank and rocks; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “WR”; and<br>(ii) “P”; and<br>(iii) a microscopic “P”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>150</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R51</td>
<td>A design consisting of a circular border in the foreground enclosing a representation of a swan on the surface of stylised water in the background, and the following:<br>(a) “THE XOZ 9999 AUSTRALIAN” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(b) “GOLD SWAN”; and<br>(c) “AH”; and<br>(d) “P”; and<br>(e) a microscopic “P”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>151</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R52</td>
<td>The same as for item 150, except omit paragraph (b) and substitute:<br>(b) “SILVER SWAN”; and</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>152</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R53</td>
<td>The same as for item 151, except the representation of a swan on the surface of stylised water is coloured.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>153</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R54</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a circular border immediately inside the rim; and<br>(b) partially obscuring that border, representations of flowers and foliage; and<br>(c) amongst the flowers and foliage, a coloured representation of a wombat sleeping in the dirt with a small bird on its back; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “WOMBAT”; and<br>(ii) “2023”; and<br>(iii) “Xoz 9999 SILVER” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(iv) “JM”; and<br>(v) “P”; and<br>(vi) a microscopic “P”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>154</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R55</td>
<td>The same as for item 153, except the representation of the wombat sleeping in the dirt with a small bird on its back is not coloured.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>155</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R56</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a partial circle enclosing a representation of 2 kookaburras perched on separate tree branches; and<br>(b) surrounding the kookaburras are waratah flowers; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “KOOKABURRA”; and<br>(ii) “2023”; and<br>(iii) “Xoz 9999 SILVER” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(iv) “WR”; and<br>(v) “P”; and<br>(vi) a coloured representation of a helmeted honeyeater enclosed in an oval; and<br>(vii) a microscopic “P”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>156</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R57</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) at the bottom of the coin and in the foreground, a representation of a coloured whale shark swimming in the ocean amongst coloured coral; and<br>(b) above the ocean, a stylised representation of waves; and<br>(c) at the top of the coin and in the background, a representation of a cloudy sky and a coloured solar eclipse; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “SR”; and<br>(ii) “P”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>

#### Division 2—Explanation of symbols

###### 3 Symbols used in Division 1

Each item of the following table contains an explanation of a symbol used in Division 1 of this Schedule to describe the shape, edge design, obverse design and reverse design of a coin.

<table>
<tr>
<td colspan="9">Explanation of symbols used in Division 1</td>
</tr>

<td colspan="2">Design Feature</td>
<td colspan="2">Symbol</td>

<td colspan="4">Dodecagonal</td>
</tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>20</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O1</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) “2023”; and<br>(d) “JC”; and<br>(e) “1952-2022”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>21</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O2</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) “2023”; and<br>(d) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(e) “JC”; and<br>(f) “1952-2022”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>22</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O3</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a representation of a rearing <i>cervus elaphus</i> (also known as a red deer) looking backward with its mouth open; and<br>(b) in the background, a representation of mantling extending out from a knight’s helmet (as depicted on the Coat of Arms of State of Queensland); and<br>(c) partially obscuring the mantling, a circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) “2023”; and<br>(iv) “JC”; and<br>(v) “1952-2022”<br>(d) also partially obscuring the mantling, a Maltese cross surmounted with St Edward’s Crown; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “AUDAX AT FIDELIS”; and<br>(ii) “X OUNCE .999 Ag” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>23</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O4</td>
<td colspan="4">The same as for item 22, except omit subparagraph (e)(ii) and substitute:<br>(ii) “X OUNCE .9999 Au” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>24</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O5</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of a circular border with a cross-hatching pattern surrounding an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) “2023”; and<br>(d) Arabic numerals of the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS”, or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(e) “PURE AUSTRALIAN GOLD”; and<br>(f) “JC”; and<br>(g) “1952-2022”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>25</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O6</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II; and the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) “JC”; and<br>(iv) “1952-2022”<br>(b) surrounding the central circle, a stylistic representation of fast flowing water, fan palm fronds and vines, and rock formations; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “X OUNCE .9999 GOLD” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed in words).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>26</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O7</td>
<td colspan="4">The same as for item 25, except omit subparagraph (c)(i) and substitute:<br>(i) “X OUNCE FINE SILVER” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed in words).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>27</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O8</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of an effigy of King Charles III and the following:<br>(a) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(d) “DT”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>28</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O9</td>
<td colspan="4">The same as for item 21, except omit paragraph (c) and substitute:<br>(c) “2024”; and</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>29</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O10</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of an effigy of King Charles III and the following:<br>(a) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(d) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(e) “DT”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>30</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O11</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 20, except omit paragraph (c) and substitute:<br>(c) “2024”; and</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>31</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O12</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) “2024”; and<br>(d) “IRB”; and<br>(e) “1952-2022”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>32</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O13</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) “2024”; and<br>(d) “RDM”; and<br>(e) “1952-2022”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>33</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O14</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II, designed by Arnold Machin, and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) “2024”; and<br>(d) “1952-2022”.</td>

</tr>

<td colspan="2">O15</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) “2024”; and<br>(d) “MG”; and<br>(e) “1952-2022”.</td>

<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a partial circle enclosing a representation of a bounding kangaroo on rocky ground next to a stream; and<br>(b) in the background, a representation of a water tank and a multi‑blade wind-powered water pump; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “KANGAROO”; and<br>(ii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iii) “Xoz 9999 GOLD” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(iv) “WR”; and<br>(v) “P125”; and<br>(vi) a microscopic “P”.</td>

Currency (Australian Coins) Determination 2019

made under the *Currency Act 1965*

**Compilation No. 106**

**Compilation date:** 30 September 2026

**Includes amendments:** *Currency (Australian Coins) Amendment (2026 Royal Australian Mint No. 10) Determination 2026*

This compilation is in 2 volumes

Volume 1: sections 1–5

Schedules 2019 to 2023

**Volume 2: Schedule 2024 to 2026**

**Endnotes**

Each volume has its own contents

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of the *Currency (Australian Coins) Determination 2019* that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 30 September 2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the ***endnotes***) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au). The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. For more information on any uncommenced amendments, see the Register for the compiled law.

**Application, saving and transitional provisions for provisions and amendments**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. For more information on any modifications, see the Register for the compiled law.

**Self‑repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

<td>20</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O1</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of an effigy of King Charles III and the following:<br>(a) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(d) “DT”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>21</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O2</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 20, except omit paragraph (d) and substitute:<br>(d) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(e) “DT”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>30</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O11</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle enclosing an effigy of King Charles III and the following:<br>(i) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(v) “DT”.<br>(b) surrounding that central circle, an ornamental border comprising stylised representations of splashing water; and<br>(c) immediately inside the rim of the coin, a stylised representation of the following:<br>(i) a rat; and<br>(ii) a pig; and<br>(iii) a dog; and<br>(iv) a rooster; and<br>(v) a monkey; and<br>(vi) a goat; and<br>(vii) a horse; and<br>(viii) a snake; and<br>(ix) a dragon; and<br>(x) a rabbit; and<br>(xi) a tiger; and<br>(xii) an ox; and<br>(d) the animal mentioned in paragraph (c) that relates to the relevant zodiac year appearing at the top of the coin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>50</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O31</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(a) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) “2024”; and<br>(d) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(e) “JC”; and<br>(f) “1952-2022”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>51</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O32</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle enclosing an effigy of Queen Elizabeth II and the following:<br>(i) “ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) “2024”; and<br>(iv) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(v) “JC”; and<br>(vi) “1952-2022”; and<br>(b) surrounding that central circle, an ornamental border comprising stylised representations of splashing water; and<br>(c) immediately inside the rim of the coin, a stylised representation of the following<br>(i) a rat; and<br>(ii) a pig; and<br>(iii) a dog; and<br>(iv) a rooster; and<br>(v) a monkey; and<br>(vi) a goat; and<br>(vii) a horse; and<br>(viii) a snake; and<br>(ix) a dragon; and<br>(x) a rabbit; and<br>(xi) a tiger; and<br>(xii) an ox; and<br>(d) the animal mentioned in paragraph (c) that relates to the relevant zodiac year appearing at the top of the coin.</td>
</tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>100</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R1</td>
<td colspan="2">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the background, a stylised representation of the chevrons from the National Rugby League (NRL) Women’s Premiership logo; and<br>(b) in the foreground, and partially obscuring the chevrons, a stylised representation of the NRL Women’s Premiership Trophy; and<br>(c) immediately inside the rim, a teal-coloured ring over a pattern of chevrons; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “2024 NATIONAL RUGBY LEAGUE WOMEN’S PREMIERSHIP”.</td>

#### Division 2—Explanation of symbols

###### 5 Symbols used in Division 1

Each item of the following table contains an explanation of a symbol used in Division 1 of this Schedule to describe the shape, edge design, obverse design and reverse design of a coin.

<tr>
<td>20</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O1</td>
<td>A design consisting of an effigy of King Charles III, and the following:<br>(a) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars and cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(d) “DT”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>22</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O3</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except the rim of the coin is gold-plated.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>23</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O4</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, but with the effigy of King Charles III instead superimposed over a textured finish.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>24</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O5</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except omit paragraph (d), substitute:<br>(d) “Xoz 9999 Au” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(e) “DT”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>25</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O6</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except the obverse, apart from the effigy of King Charles III, is gold-plated.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>26</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O7</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except omit paragraph (d), substitute:<br>(d) “Xoz 9999 Ag” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(e) “DT”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>27</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O8</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except omit paragraph (d), substitute:<br>(d) “DT”; and<br>(e) a representation of an eagle landing on a tree branch enclosed in a circle.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>28</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O9</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except omit paragraph (d), and substitute:<br>(d) “Xoz 9995 Pt” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(e) “DT”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>29</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O10</td>
<td>The same as for item 26, but with the effigy of King Charles III instead superimposed over a textured finish.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>30</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O11</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, but with the effigy of King Charles III instead superimposed over a pattern of converging lines.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>31</td>

<td>256</td>

<td>R157</td>
<td colspan="2">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a partial circular border enclosing a stylised representation of 2 kangaroos bounding over rippling water; and<br>(b) in the background, a stylised representation of mountains on the horizon; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “40” enclosed in a circle; and<br>(ii) “KANGAROO”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) “Xoz 9999 GOLD” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(v) “NH”; and<br>(vi) “P”; and<br>(vii) a microscopic “P”.</td>

<td>20</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O1</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of an effigy of King Charles III and the following:<br>(a) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(d) “DT”.</td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>21</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O2</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of an effigy of King Charles III and the following:<br>(a) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(d) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(e) “DT”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>30</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O11</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle enclosing an effigy of King Charles III and the following:<br>(i) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(v) “DT”.<br>(b) surrounding that central circle, an ornamental border comprising stylised representations of splashing water; and<br>(c) immediately inside the rim of the coin, a stylised representation of the following:<br>(i) a rat; and<br>(ii) a pig; and<br>(iii) a dog; and<br>(iv) a rooster; and<br>(v) a monkey; and<br>(vi) a goat; and<br>(vii) a horse; and<br>(viii) a snake; and<br>(ix) a dragon; and<br>(x) a rabbit; and<br>(xi) a tiger; and<br>(xii) an ox; and<br>(d) the animal mentioned in paragraph (c) that relates to the relevant zodiac year appearing at the top of the coin.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>100</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R1</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of the <i>Big Merino</i> sculpture by Attila and Louis Mokany, Gary Dutallis, and Glenn Senner, and a gift shop, upon a rock platform, with tufts of grass; and<br>(b) in the background, the following stylised sights from the town of Goulburn, New South Wales:<br>(i) a winding road; and<br>(ii) a landscape consisting of the sun, clouds, and a hill; and<br>(iii) a road sign displaying the name “GOULBURN”; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “THE BIG MERINO”; and<br>(ii) “AS”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>101</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R2</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of the <i>Big Golden Guitar</i> sculpture by Harry Frost and Len Surtees, upon a tiled platform, with trees, the Golden Guitar Tourist Centre and the Golden Guitar Motor Inn; and<br>(b) in the background, the following stylised sights from the town of Tamworth, New South Wales:<br>(i) a winding road; and<br>(ii) a landscape consisting of the sun, a cloud, and a hill; and<br>(iii) a road sign displaying the name “TAMWORTH”; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “THE BIG GOLDEN GUITAR”; and<br>(ii) “AS”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>102</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R3</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of the <i>Big Penguin</i> sculpture, upon a tiled platform; and<br>(b) in the background, the following stylised sights from the town of Penguin, Tasmania:<br>(i) set behind a tree, a grassy outlook, and a fence, the Bass Strait; and<br>(ii) a winding road; and<br>(iii) a landscape consisting of the sun, a cloud, a hill, and a flying seagull; and<br>(iv) a road sign displaying the name “PENGUIN”; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “The Big Penguin”; and<br>(ii) “AS”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>103</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R4</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of the <i>Big Galah</i> sculpture by Roger, Dianne, Allan, Quentin, Dion and Arlene Venning, upon a rock platform, with a log fence; and<br>(b) in the background, the following stylised sights from the town of Kimba, South Australia:<br>(i) the Halfway Across Australia Gem Shop, surrounded by shrubs and trees; and<br>(ii) a landscape consisting of the sun, boulders, and hills; and<br>(iii) a winding road; and<br>(iv) a motorhome driving along the winding road; and<br>(v) a triangular road sign on the side of the winding road; and<br>(vi) a road sign displaying the name “KIMBA”; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “The Big Galah”; and<br>(ii) “AS”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>104</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R5</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of the <i>Big Rocking Horse</i> sculpture by David McIntosh, surrounded by trees, shrubs, rocks and the Toy Factory; and<br>(b) in the background, the following stylised sights from the town of Gumeracha, South Australia:<br>(i) a winding road; and<br>(ii) a car driving along the winding road; and<br>(iii) a landscape consisting of the sun, boulders, and hills; and<br>(iv) a road sign displaying the name “GUMERACHA”; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “The Big Rocking Horse”; and<br>(ii) “AS”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>105</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R6</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of the <i>Big Wheelbarrow</i> sculpture by the Wedgefield Association and volunteers; and<br>(b) in the background, the following stylised sights from the town of Wedgefield, Western Australia:<br>(i) a winding road; and<br>(ii) a windmill; and<br>(iii) a landscape consisting of boulders, shrubs, hills, a cloud and the sun; and<br>(iv) a road sign displaying the name “WEDGEFIELD” with a tuft of grass at the base of the road sign; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “The Big WHEELBARROW”; and<br>(ii) “AS”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>106</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R7</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of the <i>Big Prawn</i> sculpture by James Martin, upon a pedestal; and<br>(b) in the background, the following stylised sights from the town of Exmouth, Western Australia:<br>(i) a winding road; and<br>(ii) palm trees; and<br>(iii) a landscape consisting of boulders, a hill, shrubs, a cloud and the sun; and<br>(iv) a road sign displaying the name “EXMOUTH”; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “THE BIG PRAWN”; and<br>(ii) “AS”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>107</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R8</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of the <i>Big Strawberry</i> sculpture by Michael, Lorraine, Darren and Tania Hayes, Bruce Mactier and Len Price, upon a grassy platform, with a log fence; and<br>(b) in the background, the following stylised sights from the town of Koonoomoo, Victoria:<br>(i) a winding road; and<br>(ii) a car driving along the winding road; and<br>(iii) a landscape consisting of hills, a tuft of grass, a cloud, the sun, shrubs and a house sitting on a piece of land; and<br>(iv) a road sign displaying the name “KOONOOMOO” with a tuft of grass and rocks at the base of the road sign; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “THE BIG STRAWBERRY”; and<br>(ii) “AS”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>108</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R9</td>
<td colspan="4">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of the <i>Big Barramundi</i> sculpture by Techy Masero, upon a platform, with a rock at the base of the sculpture; and<br>(b) in the background, the following stylised sights from the town of Wanguri, Northern Territory:<br>(i) a winding road; and<br>(ii) a landscape consisting of sunset, boulders, hills, clouds, a tree, shrubs, a house and a water tank; and<br>(iii) a road sign displaying the name “WANGURI”; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “THE BIG BARRAMUNDI”; and<br>(ii) “AS”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>109</td>

<tr>
<td>110</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R11</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the centre of the coin, a circular Australian gem inset representing a map of Australia; and<br>(b) surrounding that gem inset, a plain border; and<br>(c) surrounding that plain border is a representation of a desert landscape of sand, rocks and a cloudy sky, and representations of the following Australian animals:<br>(i) a cockatoo; and<br>(ii) a dingo; and<br>(iii) a snake; and<br>(iv) a thorny devil; and<br>(v) an ant; and<br>(vi) a scorpion; and<br>(vii) a bilby; and<br>(viii) a bearded dragon; and<br>(ix) a rock wallaby; and<br>(d) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(e) “Xoz 9999 SILVER” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(f) “AH”; and<br>(g) “P”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>111</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R12</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a coloured stylised representation of 3 honey bees; and<br>(b) a stylised representation of <i>rhodanthe chlorocephala</i> (also known as everlasting flowers), one of which is coloured; and<br>(c) in the background, partially obscured by the bees and flowers, a representation of a honeycomb with bees; and<br>(d) a stylised ribbon banner with the inscription “HONEY BEE”; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(ii) “Xoz 9999 SILVER” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(iii) “JM”; and<br>(iv) “P”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>112</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R13</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the centre of the coin, a circular inset opal incorporating a stylised representation of a horse; and<br>(b) surrounding the inset opal, a plain border; and<br>(c) surrounding the plain border, a representation of <i>tagetes</i> (also known as marigold flowers) with foliage; and<br>(d) immediately inside the rim, a stylised Chinese themed border; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “YEAR OF THE HORSE”; and<br>(ii) the Chinese language character (馬), pronounced <i>mǎ</i> under the Pinyin system and meaning horse; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) “Xoz 9999 SILVER” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(v) “AH”; and<br>(vi) “P”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>113</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R14</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) stylised representations of a feather, 3 coloured emu chicks, and a coloured emu, in Australian Indigenous dot painting style by Indigenous artist Chern’ee Sutton; and<br>(b) surrounding the emus is a pattern of dots, lines and circles (some of which are coloured) representing the water, land and sky; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(ii) “CS”; and<br>(iii) “P”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>114</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R15</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a coloured stylised representation of 3 quokkas on uneven ground, one standing on its hind legs and the other 2 crouching down; and<br>(b) surrounding the quokkas, a coloured stylised representation of the plant <i>trachymene coerulea</i> (also known as Rottnest Island daisies) and the plant <i>carpobrotus glaucescens</i> (also known as pig face); and<br>(c) in the background, and partially obscured by the quokkas, a stylised representation of a cloudy sky, a coloured coastline featuring the ocean, and a coloured lighthouse on a rocky headland; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “QUOKKA”; and<br>(ii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iii) “NM”; and<br>(iv) “P”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>115</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R16</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a pattern of dots immediately inside the rim of the coin forming a circle; and<br>(b) a representation of St George and the dragon, inspired by the legend as depicted in coins, paintings and engravings over the centuries; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(ii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iii) “JM”; and<br>(iv) “P”.</td>

<tr>
<td>116</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R17</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) a circular border in the foreground enclosing a representation of a swan flapping its wings, standing in a shallow body of stylised rippling water with flowers and foliage; and<br>(b) in the background, and enclosed by the circular border, a stylised representation of mountains, the rising sun and the sky; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “SILVER SWAN”; and<br>(ii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iii) “XOZ 9999” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(iv) “AUSTRALIAN”; and<br>(v) “AH”; and<br>(vi) “P”.</td>

<tr>
<td>117</td>

<tr>

<tr>
<td>120</td>

<tr>

<td>The same as for item 225, except omit subparagraphs (c)(i) to (vi), substitute:<br>(i) “SILVER SWAN”; and<br>(ii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iii) “XOZ 9999” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(iv) ‘AUSTRALIAN”; and<br>(v) “AH”; and<br>(vi) “P10”; and<br>(vii) a microscopic “P”.</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td>231</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td>R132</td>
<td>A design consisting of:<br>(a) immediately inside the rose gold-plated rim of the coin, a stylised representation of the following:<br>(i) 7 kangaroos bounding over uneven ground; and<br>(ii) clouds; and<br>(iii) a gold-plated rising sun; and<br>(b) in the background, is a rose gold-plated sky; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(ii) “JM”; and<br>(iii) “P”.</td>
</tr>
