<tr>
<td>20</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O1</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of an effigy of King Charles III and the following:<br>(a) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(d) “DT”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>21</td>
<td colspan="2">Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O2</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of an effigy of King Charles III and the following:<br>(a) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(d) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(e) “DT”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>30</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O11</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle enclosing an effigy of King Charles III and the following:<br>(i) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(ii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iii) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year; and<br>(iv) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denominations of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(v) “DT”; and<br>(b) surrounding that central circle, an ornamental border comprising stylised representations of splashing water; and<br>(c) immediately inside the rim of the coin, a stylised representation of the following:<br>(i) a rat; and<br>(ii) a pig; and<br>(iii) a dog; and<br>(iv) a rooster; and<br>(v) a monkey; and<br>(vi) a goat; and<br>(vii) a horse; and<br>(viii) a snake; and<br>(ix) a dragon; and<br>(x) a rabbit; and<br>(xi) a tiger; and<br>(xii) an ox; and<br>(d) the animal mentioned in paragraph (c) that relates to the relevant zodiac year appearing at the top of the coin.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>50</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td colspan="2">O31</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) at the top of the coin, a circle enclosing an effigy of King Charles III; and<br>(b) towards the centre of the coin, partially obscured by the effigy, a representation of the obverse of the original 19th century Holey Dollar; and<br>(c) the following:<br>(i) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(ii) the denomination of the coin in words, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(iii) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(iv) the inscription, in Arabic numerals, of a year.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>100</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R1</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a stylised representation of a female athlete performing a movement associated with a gymnastics event; and<br>(b) a central circle enclosing a yellow 7-pointed star representing the Commonwealth Star (also known as the Star of Federation) against a background of teal; and<br>(c) surrounding the pattern are 2 concentric circles (which are partially obscuring, and obscured by, the athlete) containing:<br>(i) the words “COMMONWEALTH GAMES” in one of the concentric circles; and<br>(ii) the words “TEAM AUS” in the other concentric circle; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “AWB”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>101</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R2</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a stylised representation of a male athlete in a wheelchair performing a movement associated with a 3 × 3 wheelchair basketball event; and<br>(b) a central circle enclosing a teal 7-pointed star representing the Commonwealth Star (also known as the Star of Federation) against a background of green; and<br>(c) surrounding the pattern are 2 concentric circles (which are partially obscuring, and obscured by, the athlete) containing:<br>(i) the words “COMMONWEALTH GAMES” in one of the concentric circles; and<br>(ii) the words “TEAM AUS” in the other concentric circle; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “AWB”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>102</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R3</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a stylised representation of a male athlete performing a movement associated with an athletics event; and<br>(b) a central circle enclosing a teal 7-pointed star representing the Commonwealth Star (also known as the Star of Federation) against a background of yellow; and<br>(c) surrounding the pattern are 2 concentric circles (which are partially obscuring, and obscured by, the athlete) containing:<br>(i) the words “COMMONWEALTH GAMES” in one of the concentric circles; and<br>(ii) the words “TEAM AUS” in the other concentric circle; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “AWB”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>103</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R4</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) 3 unevenly divided sections, each enclosing one of the following:<br>(i) a stylised representation of a landscape consisting of a grassy plain, shrubs and rolling hills with, in the foreground, a representation of a line of 5 soldiers, in uniform, viewed from behind, looking towards the rolling hills, with one of the soldiers partially obscured by the rim of the coin; and<br>(ii) a geometric pattern of poppy and wattle flowers, inspired by Korean traditional architecture; and<br>(iii) the number “50”; and<br>(b) the following:<br>(i) “APRIL 1951”; and<br>(ii) “BATTLE OF KAPYONG”; and<br>(iii) “37°52’36”N” and “127°31’48”E” (which are the geographical coordinates to the site of the Battle of Kapyong fought from 22 to 27 April 1951); and<br>(iv) “BS”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>104</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R5</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 103, except the design also includes a stylised representation of an envelope.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>105</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R6</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a representation of a soldier standing on a column holding and pointing a mounted gun at the sky, with the soldier’s body partially obscured by the column, and the lower part of the column (which is partially obscured by the rim of the coin) forming a stylised representation of the number “20”; and<br>(b) at the top of the coin, a representation of 5 Junkers Ju 52 aircraft flying in formation, viewed from below, and representations of 4 paratroopers in midair, with one of the paratroopers partially obscuring another of the paratroopers; and<br>(c) in the background, and partially obscured by the soldier, column and mounted gun, a representation of a section of a fragment of a destroyed building and the stylised representation of 8 people standing in a row, with each person representing one of the following:<br>(i) a soldier, in uniform, with his left arm in a sling and his right arm behind his back; and<br>(ii) a female nurse wearing a dress and headdress, with her arms clasped behind her back; and<br>(iii) a male navy sailor, in uniform, with his arms clasped behind his back; and<br>(iv) a male farmer wearing a shirt, pants and a cap, with his arms clasped behind his back; and<br>(v) a male soldier, in uniform, holding a rifle at rest which is pointing to the left; and<br>(vi) a female nurse wearing a dress and headdress, with her arms clasped behind her back; and<br>(vii) a male farmer wearing a shirt with rolled up sleeves, pants and a cap, and holding a farming tool; and<br>(viii) a male soldier, in uniform, holding a rifle at rest which is pointing to the right; and<br>(d) partially obscured by the rim of the coin, 2 blue- and 1 white-coloured rectangular shapes (representing the colours of the Greek flag); and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “GREECE & CRETE”; and<br>(ii) “1941”; and<br>(iii) “AB” (in a stylised form).</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>106</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R7</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 105, except the design also includes a stylised representation of an envelope.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>107</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R8</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) partially obscured by the rim of the coin, a representation of a Hawker Hurricane aircraft in flight, viewed from above; and<br>(b) partially obscured by the rim of the coin, a representation of a warship, viewed from the side, based on the Royal Australian Navy’s Scott Class Destroyer Flotilla Leader warship ‘HMAS Stuart’; and<br>(c) a representation of an Ordnance QF 25-pounder field gun; and<br>(d) partially obscured by the rim of the coin, red-, yellow-, dark blue- and light blue-coloured parallelogram shapes (representing the colours of the British and Commonwealth military award, the Africa Star); and<br>(e) in the background and on the right of the coin, and partially obscured by the aircraft, field gun and yellow-coloured parallelogram shape, a geometric pattern of various shapes, inspired by the architectural style of tiles commonly found in the regions of North Africa and the Middle East; and<br>(f) the following:<br>(i) “20”; and<br>(ii) “NORTH AFRICA”; and<br>(iii) “MIDDLE EAST”; and<br>(iv) “1941”; and<br>(v) “AB” (in stylised form).</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>108</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R9</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 107, except the design also includes a stylised representation of an envelope.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>109</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R10</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, and partially obscured by the rim of the coin, a stylised representation of a standing female telegraphist, viewed from the side, wearing a skirt, jacket and headphones, and operating a telegraph key, with the skirt forming a stylised representation of the number “20”; and<br>(b) a stylised representation of a female mechanic, viewed from the side, wearing a work shirt, pants and a cap, holding a spanner in her left hand and standing on a platform behind a handrail next to an aircraft propellor, with the propellor partially obscuring the platform and handrail and partially obscured by the mechanic, telegraphist and rim of the coin; and<br>(c) behind, and partially obscured by, the mechanic, platform, handrail and propellor, a stylised representation of another aircraft propellor (which is also partially obscured by the rim of the coin); and<br>(d) a stylised representation of a female clerk, wearing a shirt and tie, sitting behind a desk operating a typewriter with paper protruding from it, with a lamp on the desk and a poster containing a map of Australia on the wall behind the desk, with the poster partially obscured by the clerk and typewriter; and<br>(e) partially obscuring the telegraphist, mechanic and propellors, representations of “AWAS”, “WRAN” and “WAAAF” in Morse code; and<br>(f) coloured shapes representing the uniform colours of the Women’s Auxiliary Australian Air Force, including a yellow-coloured circle and dark blue- and light blue-coloured oblongs, with the oblongs partially obscured by the rim of the coin; and<br>(g) the following:<br>(i) "WOMEN’S SERVICES”; and<br>(ii) “1941”; and<br>(iii) “AB” (in a stylised form).</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>110</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R11</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 109, except the design also includes a stylised representation of an envelope.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>111</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R12</td>
<td colspan="3">A design, replicating the original 1927 Canberra florin designed by George Kruger Gray, consisting of a pattern of 100 stylised coins forming a border immediately inside the rim of the coin and enclosing the following:<br>(a) at the top of the coin, an ornamental scroll enclosing a representation of Old Parliament House in Canberra, Australian Capital Territory; and<br>(b) below the ornamental scroll, a representation of 2 crossed maces which is partially obscured by another ornamental scroll bearing the inscription “1927”; and<br>(c) immediately inside the border, 2 stars and 2 dots; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “AUSTRALIAN COMMEMORATIVE COINS”; and<br>(ii) “1927-2027”; and<br>(iii) “K.G.” (in a stylised form).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>112</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R13</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a central circle containing a coloured pattern of concentric circles graduating from shades of orange to purple (moving from the centre of the coin outwards); and<br>(b) to the left of the central circle, a stylised representation of a soldier in uniform, standing and facing right, holding and playing a bugle; and<br>(c) partially obscured by the soldier and central circle, a stylised outline of a war memorial surrounded by a textured pattern; and<br>(d) in the bottom half of the coin, and partially obscuring the textured pattern, a stylised outline of steps ascending to the right; and<br>(e) in the top half of the coin surrounding the central circle, and partially obscured by the war memorial and soldier, a representation of 2 musical staves with notes forming two concentric semicircles, representing a section of the musical score of the military bugle call known as the ‘Last Post’; and<br>(f) the following inscriptions:<br>(i) “THE LAST POST”; and<br>(ii) “REMEMBRANCE”; and<br>(iii) “LA” (in a stylised form).</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>113</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R14</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 112, except omit subparagraph (f)(iii) and substitute:<br>(iii) “LA” (in a stylised form); and<br>(iv) “C” (in a stylised form).</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>114</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R15</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a crescent shape partially obscured on the convex side by a stylised representation of a goat, facing right, standing on rocky ground; and<br>(b) above, and partially obscured by the goat, a stylised representation of a branch of a persimmon tree, adorned with leaves and fruit; and<br>(c) within the crescent shape, the Chinese language character (羊), pronounced <i>yáng</i> under the Pinyin system, and meaning goat; and<br>(d) the following stylised inscriptions:<br>(i) “YEAR OF THE GOAT”; and<br>(ii) “BS”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>115</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R16</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 114, except omit subparagraph (d)(ii) and substitute:<br>(ii) “Xoz .999 Ag” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(iii) “BS”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>116</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R17</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 114, except omit subparagraph (d)(ii) and substitute:<br>(ii) “Xoz .9999 Au” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(iii) “BS”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>117</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R18</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a portrait of Queen Elizabeth II at the centre of the coin; and<br>(b) above the portrait, the Royal cypher of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II surmounted with St Edward’s Crown; and<br>(c) to the left of the portrait, a stylised representation of the badge of the Auxiliary Territorial Service; and<br>(d) surrounding the portrait, stylised representations of roses, myrtle, lily of the valley, and golden wattle flowers and sprigs; and<br>(e) intertwined in the flowers and sprigs, stylised representations of the following:<br>(i) 2 theatrical masks (Thalia and Melpomene); and<br>(ii) a corgi; and<br>(iii) a horse; and<br>(iv) a painter’s palette; and<br>(f) the following:<br>(i) “CENTENARY OF THE BIRTH OF HER MAJESTY QUEEN ELIZABETH II”; and<br>(ii) “AS”; and<br>(iii) the letter “C” enclosed in a square.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>118</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R19</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) immediately inside the rim, an ornamental border, inspired by traditional Chinese knotting; and<br>(b) in the foreground, a stylised representation of a goat standing on a pile of rocks; and<br>(c) partially obscured by the goat and partially obscuring the pile of rocks, stylised representations of 3 <i>Narcissus tazetta</i> plants (commonly known as Chinese sacred lily); and<br>(d) above the goat, the Chinese language character (羊), pronounced <i>yáng</i> under the Pinyin system, and meaning goat; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) a stylised representation of the designer’s initials “LA”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>119</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R20</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 118, except the design also includes a stylised representation of an envelope.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>120</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R21</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) towards the centre of the coin, a representation of the reverse of the original 19th century Holey Dollar; and<br>(b) in the foreground, partially obscuring the representation of the Holey Dollar, a representation of the obverse of the original 19th century Dump coin; and<br>(c) at the bottom of the Holey Dollar, and to the left of the Dump coin, a representation of a ribbon curled around the flowers, buds and leaves of the <i>Dahlia pinnata</i> plant (commonly known as the dahlia), the floral emblem of Mexico; and<br>(d) at the bottom of the representation of the Holey Dollar, and to the right of the Dump coin, a representation of a ribbon curled around the flowers, branches and leaves of an <i>Acacia pycnantha</i> plant (commonly known as golden wattle), the floral emblem of Australia; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “ORIGINS OF AUSTRALIAN COIN”; and<br>(ii) “EW” (in a stylised form).</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>121</td>
<td colspan="2">Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R22</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a stylised representation of a platypus; and<br>(b) a combination of circles, tear drop shapes, and irregular shapes incorporated into the representation of the platypus; and<br>(c) behind the platypus, a combination of tubular and irregular shapes stacked horizontally; and<br>(d) surrounding the platypus, coloured tear drop shapes and circles; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “50”; and<br>(ii) “AWB”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>122</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R23</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a circular border immediately inside the rim; and<br>(b) in the foreground, partially obscuring the border, stylised representations of the following:<br>(i) a female pastoralist riding a horse; and<br>(ii) a border collie (a breed of British herding dog); and<br>(iii) a flying wedge-tailed eagle with its wings outstretched; and<br>(iv) Spinifex grass; and<br>(c) in the background, partially obscured by the border, stylised representations of the following:<br>(i) a rangeland landscape featuring other grasses, rolling hills and a eucalyptus tree; and<br>(ii) to the left of the pastoralist and horse, a cow and 2 sheep standing together; and<br>(d) the following:<br>(i) “RANGELANDS AND PASTORALISTS”; and<br>(ii) “AWB”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>123</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R24</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 122, except the design also includes a stylised representation of an envelope.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>124</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R25</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of stylised representations of:<br>(a) in the centre of the coin, a light bulb containing a stylised outline of a map of Australia, surrounded by rays of light; and<br>(b) below, and partially obscuring the light bulb, a stump‑jump plough (also titled the “Vixen”); and<br>(c) partially obscured by the stump-jump plough, an open pie iron (also known as a jaffle maker or sandwich toaster); and<br>(d) partially obscured by the jaffle maker, an oscilloscope; and<br>(e) partially obscured by the stump-jump plough, a baby capsule; and<br>(f) partially obscured by the baby capsule, a flight recorder (also known as a “black box”); and<br>(g) 6 stars; and<br>(h) the following:<br>(i) “AUSTRALIAN INVENTIONS”.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>125</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R26</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 124, except the design also includes a stylised representation of a light bulb, enclosed in a square.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>126</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R27</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of an open pie iron (also known as a jaffle maker or sandwich toaster); and<br>(b) partially obscured by the rim of the coin, a stylised representation of a jaffle or toasted sandwich, with melted cheese dripping from it; and<br>(c) a stylised representation of a small portion of cheese enclosed in a reticle; and<br>(d) a stylised representation of a small loaf of bread enclosed in a reticle; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “JAFFLE MAKER”; and<br>(ii) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>127</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R28</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 126, except the design also includes a stylised representation of a light bulb, enclosed in a square.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>128</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R29</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of a baby capsule; and<br>(b) partially obscured by the rim of the coin, a stylised representation of the right-side profile of a crash test baby dummy’s head, neck and chest, facing towards the baby capsule; and<br>(c) above the baby capsule, a stylised representation of a small car seat with a seat belt enclosed in a reticle; and<br>(d) above the car seat, a stylised representation of a small car enclosed in a reticle; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “BABY SAFETY CAPSULE”; and<br>(ii) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>129</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R30</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 128, except the design also includes a stylised representation of a light bulb, enclosed in a square.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>130</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R31</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) a stylised representation of the Parkes radio telescope ‘Murriyang’; and<br>(b) in the foreground, a stylised representation of an oscilloscope; and<br>(c) above the radio telescope and oscilloscope, a stylised representation of 2 small laptops, with curved lines representing radio wave signals between them, enclosed in a reticle; and<br>(d) above the oscilloscope, a stylised representation of radio waves enclosed in a reticle; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “WLAN”; and<br>(ii) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>131</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R32</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 130, except the design also includes a stylised representation of a light bulb, enclosed in a square.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>132</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R33</td>
<td colspan="3">A design consisting of:<br>(a) in the foreground, a stylised representation of a stump‑jump plough (also titled the “Vixen”); and<br>(b) to the left of the stump-jump plough, stylised representations of 3 ears of wheat; and<br>(c) above the stump-jump plough, a stylised representation of a plant, with its roots below rocky ground, enclosed in a reticle; and<br>(d) 3 non-straight lines representing dirt enclosed in a reticle; and<br>(e) the following:<br>(i) “STUMP JUMP PLOUGH”; and<br>(ii) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars or cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>133</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R34</td>
<td colspan="3">The same as for item 132, except the design also includes a stylised representation of a light bulb, enclosed in a square.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>134</td>
<td>Reverse</td>
<td colspan="2">R35</td>

#### Division 2—Explanation of symbols

###### 5 Symbols used in Division 1

Each item of the following table contains an explanation of a symbol used in Division 1 of this Schedule to describe the shape, edge design, obverse design and reverse design of a coin.

<table>
<tr>
<td colspan="4">Explanation of symbols used in Division 1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>Design Feature</td>
<td>Symbol</td>
<td>Explanation</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1</td>
<td>Shape</td>
<td>S1</td>
<td>Circular</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8</td>
<td>Shape</td>
<td>S8</td>
<td>Rectangular with rounded corners</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>13</td>
<td>Shape</td>
<td>S13</td>
<td>Annular</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>15</td>
<td>Edge</td>
<td>E1</td>
<td>Continuously milled</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>16</td>
<td>Edge</td>
<td>E2</td>
<td>Plain</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>20</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O1</td>
<td>A design consisting of an effigy of King Charles III, and the following:<br>(a) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars and cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLARS”, “DOLLAR” or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(d) “DT”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>23</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O4</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, but with the effigy of King Charles III instead superimposed over a textured finish.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>24</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O5</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except omit paragraph (d), substitute:<br>(d) “Xoz 9999 Au” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(e) “DT”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>25</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O6</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except the obverse, apart from the effigy of King Charles III, is gold-plated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>26</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O7</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except omit paragraph (d), substitute:<br>(d) “Xoz 9999 Ag” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(e) “DT”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>28</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O9</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except omit paragraph (d), and substitute:<br>(d) “Xoz 9995 Pt” (where “X” is the nominal weight in ounces of the coin, expressed as a whole number or a common fraction in Arabic numerals); and<br>(e) “DT”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>30</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O11</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, but with the effigy of King Charles III instead superimposed over a pattern of converging lines.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>31</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O12</td>
<td>The same as for item 26, but with the effigy of King Charles III superimposed over a square.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>36</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O17</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except immediately inside the rim of the coin is a pattern of wavy lines surrounding a circle that incorporates the effigy of King Charles III.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>38</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O19</td>
<td>A design consisting of a circular pattern of stylised stars and dots, an effigy of King Charles III, and the following:<br>(a) “CHARLES III”; and<br>(b) “AUSTRALIA”; and<br>(c) Arabic numerals for the amount, in dollars and cents, of the denomination of the coin, followed by “DOLLAR”, “DOLLARS”, or “CENTS” as the case requires; and<br>(d) “DT”.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>39</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O20</td>
<td>The same as for item 26, except the effigy of King Charles III is superimposed over a square of radial lines.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>40</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O21</td>
<td>The same as for item 24, except the effigy of King Charles III is superimposed over a square of radial lines.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>42</td>
<td>Obverse</td>
<td>O23</td>
<td>The same as for item 20, except the effigy is enclosed in a circular border.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>43</td>

## Endnotes

### Endnote 1—About the endnotes

The endnotes provide information about this compilation and the compiled law.

The following endnotes are included in every compilation:

Endnote 1—About the endnotes

Endnote 2—Abbreviation key

Endnote 3—Legislation history

Endnote 4—Amendment history

**Abbreviation key—Endnote 2**

The abbreviation key sets out abbreviations that may be used in the endnotes.

**Legislation history and amendment history—Endnotes 3 and 4**

Amending laws are annotated in the legislation history and amendment history.

The legislation history in endnote 3 provides information about each law that has amended (or will amend) the compiled law. The information includes commencement details for amending laws and details of any application, saving or transitional provisions that are not included in this compilation.

The amendment history in endnote 4 provides information about amendments at the provision (generally section or equivalent) level. It also includes information about any provision of the compiled law that has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law.

**Misdescribed amendments**

A misdescribed amendment is an amendment that does not accurately describe how an amendment is to be made. If, despite the misdescription, the amendment can be given effect as intended, then the misdescribed amendment can be incorporated through an editorial change made under section 15V of the *Legislation Act 2003*.

If a misdescribed amendment cannot be given effect as intended, the amendment is not incorporated and “(md not incorp)” is added to the amendment history.
